## Mobile surveillance in California

California carries the country's most public organized retail crime problem and one of its strictest privacy regimes. Both are operational considerations for us, not slogans. We deploy with default 30-day rolling retention, customer-controlled access logs, and zero third-party data sharing. CCPA, CPRA, and AB 2273 considerations are documented in our standard California MSA.

We're active across the Bay Area, Los Angeles, San Diego, the Inland Empire, and Sacramento with 45+ units.

## Industries we protect in California

**Retail and ORC response.** Bay Area smash-and-grab incidents that hit national news in 2023 didn't stop in 2024. We deploy Mobile Surveillance Unit and Mobile Surveillance Unit around parking decks, distribution centers, and high-loss store locations for several national retail chains. SOC-monitored voice-down deterrent reduces 97% of false alarm escalation and gets PD on real incidents faster.

**Construction.** LA County multifamily, Inland Empire industrial, Bay Area infrastructure. Material theft (copper, lumber, equipment) is the baseline driver, with after-hours encampment response on urban sites in SF and LA proper.

**Licensed cannabis.** California's licensed cultivation and retail sector requires extensive video surveillance under CCR Title 16 and local jurisdiction rules. We deploy NDAA-compliant Mobile Surveillance Unit for cultivation perimeters and Mobile Surveillance Unit for retail dispensary lots, with retention configured to license requirements (typically 90 days for cannabis, longer than our default).

## Coverage and lead time

- **Bay Area, LA County, Orange County, San Diego:** 7-10 business days
- **Inland Empire, Sacramento, Central Valley:** 7-10 business days
- **Far Northern California, Eastern Sierra:** 10-14 business days

California inventory pre-stages in Ontario (Inland Empire) for SoCal and Stockton for NorCal coverage.

## A California-area deployment

A Bay Area-based developer running two podium-construction multifamily projects in Oakland and Hayward was losing roughly $11,000/month between copper, lumber, and tool theft, plus periodic encampment-related vandalism. Four Mobile Surveillance Units deployed in 8 business days. Twelve-month coverage: 67 deterred entry attempts, four arrests via SOC-dispatched Oakland PD and Hayward PD, an 84% reduction in successful theft incidents. The developer extended the contract to a third Concord site.

## California compliance and procurement

CCPA and CPRA compliance is documented in our standard California MSA. Default video retention is 30 days rolling — customers can extend with documented business purpose, never via casual request. ALPR features, where deployed, comply with California Civil Code §1798.90.5 retention and disclosure requirements.

NDAA Section 889 compliant for federally-funded California work. We hold California state cooperative purchasing credentials and Sourcewell is widely accepted by California municipalities and special districts.

faq.q: How does VDS handle CCPA data subject requests?
faq.a: Customer controls access. If an individual identified in video footage submits a data subject request to you, we provide the technical assistance needed to locate, export, or delete the relevant footage. We don't field DSR requests independently.

faq.q: Are your units compliant with California cannabis surveillance rules?
faq.a: Yes. We configure retention to local jurisdiction requirements (90 days is typical), provide license-holder access controls, and document chain of custody for any footage pulled.

faq.q: Can you deploy ALPR in California?
faq.a: Yes, with the contractual framework that satisfies §1798.90.5 — retention limits, access logs, no third-party sharing. We will not deploy ALPR without that framework executed.

faq.q: Do you work with California state procurement?
faq.a: Yes. We hold California cooperative purchasing credentials and Sourcewell is accepted by most California cities, counties, and special districts.

finalCTABody: We won't argue the privacy framework with you. We documented it because customers asked. Get a California-specific quote with the MSA attached.

These are the operators we'd point you to. Each runs Canadian infrastructure, employs Canadian staff, and handles Canadian compliance natively.

- **Spotter Security** — Toronto-based mobile and integrated security. Good fit for GTA construction and commercial sites.

We're listing competitors on our own page because honest referrals beat a bad fit. If one of these is right for you, take it.

This is where we can help today. If your portfolio spans both countries — a US retailer with stores in Ontario, a North American construction GC, a utility with assets on both sides of the border — VDS can quote and operate your US footprint while we coordinate Canadian coverage with a vetted Canadian partner.

You get one point of contact, consistent reporting on the US side, and a defensible compliance posture on the Canadian side. Talk to us before you split the contract two ways.

Before VDS deploys a Canadian unit, we need:

- AWS Canada Central data residency configured separately from our US environment
- PIPEDA-aligned data handling, plus provincial regimes (Quebec Law 25 in particular)
- French-language SOC operator coverage for Quebec deployments
- NDAA Section 889 is a US federal standard; the Canadian equivalent for federal procurement is the Policy on Government Security and related supply-chain integrity reviews. We'll address this before any Crown procurement work.

If you want a heads-up when we open Canadian operations, drop your email. We'll contact you with a launch date, regional coverage, and pricing — and only then. No drip campaign in the meantime.
